findings.title: Patch Release Update: Zimbra 10.1.20
findings.summary_md: Synacor released ZCS 10.1.20 with a permanent fix for a command injection vulnerability in the SNMP monitoring component when SNMP notifications are enabled, rated High severity with Low deployment risk. The post states this is the permanent fix for the vulnerability disclosed in Zimbra's security advisory on 26 June 2026. The same release also fixed several Classic Web Client stored XSS issues and a mail forwarding restriction bypass.

findings.title: CVE-2026-73570 Detail (NVD)
findings.summary_md: NVD published the record for CVE-2026-73570 on 2026-08-13: a remote code execution flaw in Zimbra Collaboration (ZCS) before 10.1.20 when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled. Due to improper sanitization during SNMP notification processing, an unauthenticated attacker can send specially crafted SMTP requests that execute arbitrary operating system commands as the zimbra user. CWE-78, CVSS 3.1 base score 8.9 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L).

findings.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog: CVE-2026-73570
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2026-73570 to the KEV catalog on 2026-08-21 as 'Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) OS Command Injection Vulnerability', with a patch due date of 2026-08-24 under BOD 26-04. The entry requires forensic triage of potentially affected systems; ransomware campaign use is listed as Unknown. Notes reference the Zimbra security advisories wiki, the 10.1.20 patch release blog, and the NVD entry.
